explanation: The secret treaty of April 1915 is what Italy brought to Paris and what Paris would not honour. It had promised the Trentino, Trieste, Istria, a part of Dalmatia and a share of the Ottoman and German settlements in exchange for entering the war within a month, and the peace conference set most of it aside in favour of self-determination for the South Slavs. The Italian delegation walked out in April 1919 over Fiume, which the treaty had not even promised. The claim is about the terms of the Italian quarrel at Paris, not about the whole conference, which had many other things to settle.
